requirements.requirement: On node1, run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance every day at 02:15 and append its output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log.
requirements.summary: A root-owned cron.d entry contains the exact daily 02:15 schedule and appends both stdout and stderr to the required log. crond is running and enabled, the capture path produced log entries, and the schedule and retained log survived restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged before configuration, before restart, and after restart. The implementation uses the already-installed Vixie Cron package and legacy SysV service tooling.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The exact schedule and output-retention path are configured and functional, persist across a directly observed restart, and the legacy OS and kernel remain unchanged. Provider-wide restart evidence for the sole managed node is coherent and complete.
limitations: No naturally scheduled 02:15 invocation was observed; output capture was validated through bounded manual executions of the same command and redirection path before and after restart.

The lifecycle failed-service probe is unsupported on this non-systemd platform, and its package-health probe invokes an unsupported yum operation. Executor evidence nevertheless directly shows crond healthy, while lifecycle comparisons show no package-related change.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing and securing the cron entry, creating and testing the requested append-only log path, restoring SELinux contexts, performing the mandatory restart, and running a bounded post-restart capture test all had clear task, verification, security, or protocol roles. No new temporary files, sockets, package changes, or other lifecycle residue appeared. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, acknowledged restart with observed downtime, a different post-restart identity, and recovered crond, schedule, platform, and retained log data.
